business_problem: Mears wanted to replace email-driven internal services and scattered forms with one employee-services platform so staff across housing operations could find policies, HR answers, and support quickly instead of hunting through documents or waiting on central teams.
solution_summary: Mears is positioning the ServiceNow AI Platform as the internal front door for IT, HR, and eventually finance, legal, health, and safety services. The immediate catalyst was Now Assist for IT Service Management, which layers AI Search and summarization onto the company's existing ITSM and HR Service Delivery foundation. Employees can now ask natural-language questions such as maternity-leave policies and receive instant, user-friendly summaries instead of manually searching documents, while service teams use case summarization and resolution notes to accelerate more complex requests. Mears is also extending Customer Service Management so customers can manage accounts and requests through the same platform, and it uses ServiceNow Impact to govern upgrades, roadmap decisions, and best-practice adoption. The architecture centers on a knowledge-driven self-service model that reduces phone traffic, increases portal use, and gives Mears one evolving platform for central-service modernization.

data_flow: Employees ask questions in everyday language, where Now Assist and AI Search scan company documents and return summaries or route work into IT and HR workflows. For more complex cases, service teams use AI-generated summaries and notes to continue work quickly, while the same platform is being extended to customer-service flows and governed through ServiceNow Impact.
business_outcome: Mears saves up to 10 minutes per request with Now Assist, deflects 83% of calls, increased self-service by more than 8% in the first few months, and built a stronger platform foundation for customer-service, risk, and asset-management expansion.
